You are urban_comet97, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
agents form one swarm, organized into groups. You are in group_1 with gentle_otter27, pale_lantern48, sandy_walnut42, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in
its own sandbox, on its own git repository. Your group also shares one `main` branch, which every member
can push to. Your group has a private channel (`group`) that only its members can see and post in. All
10 agents, in every group, can read and post in the public channel (`public`). Work together with
your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to coordinate within your
group, and `public` to share general findings with other groups.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Other groups cannot see your group's `main`.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is the swarm's score on this task: the highest score among all groups, where a group's score
is the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on its `main` at the end. Every agent receives the
same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents post and ask each other questions. In `group`, announce
what you are exploring, building, or have found: a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a proposal for how to organize your group's work, or a question. In `public`, share general
findings (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case) with the other groups.
- `post` publishes a message to `group` or `public`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- Who can read a pointer depends on the channel: in `group`, only your group; in `public`, every agent.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, the latest 20 posts in `public`, and any
  unopened posts that mention you, one line each (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a
  post's number shows its full text, with its pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own
  version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished in `group`, with a pointer,
  then go back to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main`
  does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve
  as many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Working with agents from other groups
- **Each group must have its own complete and runnable version of the program on its `main`.**
- `public` is a channel where you share general findings with the other groups: how the reference program
  behaves (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), edge cases worth testing, approaches that worked or did not, and code that
  others may find useful. Post what you learned that other groups are likely to miss. Keep the
  coordination of your own group's work in `group`.
- Read what others post in `public`. When a finding would improve your group's version, use it in your
  own code and test it against the reference program. Shared code is there to show how something can be
  done: take the idea or the fix you need.

Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.

- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.

# Ouch! `ouch` stands for **Obvious Unified Compression Helper**. It's a CLI tool for compressing and decompressing various formats. - [Features](#features) - [Usage](#usage) - [Installation](#installation) - [Supported Formats](#supported-formats) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Contributing](#contributing) # Features 1. Easy to use. 2. Fast. 3. Great error message feedback. 4. No runtime dependencies. 5. Accessibility mode ([see more](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Accessibility)). 6. Shell completions and man pages. # Usage `ouch` has three main subcommands: - `ouch decompress` (alias `d`) - `ouch compress` (alias `c`) - `ouch list` (alias `l` or `ls`) To see `help` for a specific command: ```sh ouch help ouch --help # equivalent ``` ## Decompressing Use the `decompress` subcommand, `ouch` will detect the extensions automatically. ```sh ouch decompress a.zip # Decompress multiple files ouch decompress a.zip b.tar.gz c.tar ``` The `-d/--dir` flag can be used to redirect decompression results to another directory. ```sh # Decompress 'summer_vacation.zip' inside of new folder 'pictures' ouch decompress summer_vacation.zip --dir pictures ``` ## Compressing Pass input files to the `compress` subcommand, add the **output file** at the end. ```sh # Compress two files into `archive.zip` ouch compress one.txt two.txt archive.zip # Compress file.txt using .lz4 and .zst ouch compress file.txt file.txt.lz4.zst ``` `ouch` detects the extensions of the **output file** to decide what formats to use. ## Listing ```sh ouch list archive.zip # Example with tree formatting ouch list source-code.zip --tree ``` Output: ``` └── src ├── archive │ ├── mod.rs │ ├── tar.rs │ └── zip.rs ├── utils │ ├── colors.rs │ ├── formatting.rs │ ├── mod.rs │ └── fs.rs ├── commands │ ├── list.rs │ ├── compress.rs │ ├── decompress.rs │ └── mod.rs ├── accessible.rs ├── error.rs ├── cli.rs └── main.rs ``` # Supported formats | Format | `.tar` | `.zip` | `.7z` | `.gz` | `.sz` | `.zst` | `.xz` | `.lzma` | `.lz` | `.bz`, `.bz2` | `.bz3` | `.lz4` | `.rar` | `.br` | |:---------:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Supported | ✓ | ✓¹ | ✓¹ | ✓² | ✓² | ✓² | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓³ | ✓ | ✓: Supports compression and decompression. ✓¹: Due to limitations of the compression format itself, (de)compression can't be done with streaming. ✓²: Supported, and compression runs in parallel. ✓³: Due to RAR's restrictive license, only decompression and listing can be supported. If you wish to exclude non-free code from your build, you can disable RAR support by building without the `unrar` feature. Aliases for these formats are also supported: - `tar`: `tgz`, `tbz`, `tbz2`, `tlz4`, `txz`, `tlzma`, `tsz`, `tzst`, `tlz`, `cbt` - `zip`: `cbz`, `epub` - `7z`: `cb7` - `rar`: `cbr` Formats can be chained: - `.tar.gz` - `.tar.gz.xz.zst.gz.lz4.sz` If the filename has no extensions, `ouch` will try to infer the format by the [file signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_file_signatures) and ask the user for confirmation. # Installation Refer to the packages list on the right. The most commonly used installation methods: ## On Arch Linux ```bash pacman -S ouch ``` ## On MacOS via Homebrew ```bash brew install ouch ``` ## On Windows via Scoop ```cmd scoop install ouch ``` ## From crates.io ```bash cargo install ouch ``` (If you're on Ubuntu, you might need to install `clang` to build it from crates.io.) ## Download the latest release bundle Check the [releases page](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/releases). Release binaries are signed with [Sigstore](https://sigstore.dev) via GitHub's artifact attestations. Verify a downloaded binary with the GitHub CLI: ``` gh attestation verify ouch-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --repo ouch-org/ouch ``` ### Reproducing a release build Release builds are reproducible. Given the source at a tagged commit, anyone can rebuild the same binary and check that it matches what we shipped. Steps: ``` git clone https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch cd ouch git checkout export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --pretty=%ct) export RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$(pwd)=." cargo build --locked --release --target ``` The toolchain version is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` and rustup will install it automatically. Cross-compiled targets (anything using `cross-rs/cross`) inherit the cross Docker image's toolchain, which is not pinned by digest yet, so those targets are bit-for-bit reproducible only against the same `cross` image release. ## Compiling from source code Check the [wiki guide on compiling](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Compiling-and-installing-from-source-code). # Benchmarks Benchmark results are available [here](benchmarks/results.md). Performance of compressing and decompressing [Rust](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust) source code is measured and compared with [Hyperfine](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine). The values presented are the average (wall clock) elapsed time. Note: `ouch` focuses heavily on usage ergonomics and nice error messages, but we plan on doing some optimization in the future. Versions used: - `ouch` _0.4.0_ - [`tar`] _1.34_ - [`unzip`][infozip] _6.00_ - [`zip`][infozip] _3.0_ # Contributing Contributions of all sizes are welcome and appreciated! - Open an [issue](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/issues). - Package it for your favorite distribution or package manager. - Share it with a friend! - Open a pull request. If you're creating a Pull Request, check [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). [`tar`]: https://www.gnu.org/software/tar/ [infozip]: http://www.info-zip.org/ #!/bin/sh # Build step run by the ProgramBench evaluator: create ./executable as a launcher for main.py. cat > executable <<'LAUNCHER' #!/bin/sh exec python3 "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/main.py" "$@" LAUNCHER chmod +x executable "}

content.text: Tree mode preserves archive insertion order, infers parent directories, and merges repeated paths; it does not sort alphabetically. I’m packaging these observed rules as a reusable listing helper while the CLI owner handles argument parsing.

name: exec
input:
const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/listing.py
+"""Archive member listing helpers for the ouch-compatible command line."""
+import os
+import tarfile
+import zipfile
+
+
+def archive_members(path):
+    """Return (name, is_directory) pairs in archive order."""
+    if zipfile.is_zipfile(path):
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
+            return [(i.filename.rstrip("/"), i.is_dir()) for i in z.infolist()]
+    try:
+        with tarfile.open(path, "r:*") as t:
+            return [(i.name.rstrip("/"), i.isdir()) for i in t.getmembers()]
+    except (tarfile.TarError, OSError):
+        return None
+
+
+def tree_lines(members):
+    """Render archive members as an insertion-ordered Unicode tree."""
+    class Node:
+        def __init__(self, name, directory=False):
+            self.name, self.directory = name, directory
+            self.children = {}
+            self.order = []
+
+    root = Node("")
+    for name, is_dir in members:
+        parts = [p for p in name.split("/") if p]
+        node = root
+        for idx, part in enumerate(parts):
+            last = idx == len(parts) - 1
+            directory = not last or is_dir
+            if part not in node.children:
+                node.children[part] = Node(part, directory)
+                node.order.append(part)
+            elif directory:
+                node.children[part].directory = True
+            node = node.children[part]
+
+    out = []
+    def walk(node, prefix):
+        for i, key in enumerate(node.order):
+            child = node.children[key]
+            final = i == len(node.order) - 1
+            out.append(prefix + ("└── " if final else "├── ") + child.name + ("/" if child.directory else ""))
+            if child.children:
+                walk(child, prefix + ("   " if final else "│  "))
+    walk(root, "")
+    return out
+
+
+def list_archive(path, tree=False):
+    """Print-compatible body lines; caller adds the Archive header."""
+    members = archive_members(path)
+    if members is None:
+        return None
+    if tree:
+        return tree_lines(members)
+    return [name + ("/" if is_dir and name else "") for name, is_dir in members]
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch);text(r)

- Single directory to `.gz` diagnostic matched.
- ZIP directory entries and tar directory member names were refined by teammates.
- Relative and absolute extensionless compression diagnostics were corrected; recent changes may have evolved after last fetch.

**Constraints/preferences:** User explicitly asked to keep using tools and continue reviewing until time runs out. They requested reference comparisons, fixes, and pushes. Python standard library only. Do not run `compile.sh`; it is evaluator owned. Keep updates concise in `commentary`, coordinate in `group`, and push all useful work to `team/main`.

Easy to use. 2. Fast. 3. Great error message feedback. 4. No runtime dependencies. 5. Accessibility mode ([see more](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Accessibility)). 6. Shell completions and man pages. # Usage `ouch` has three main subcommands: - `ouch decompress` (alias `d`) - `ouch compress` (alias `c`) - `ouch list` (alias `l` or `ls`) To see `help` for a specific command: ```sh ouch help ouch --help # equivalent ``` ## Decompressing Use the `decompress` subcommand, `ouch` will detect the extensions automatically. ```sh ouch decompress a.zip # Decompress multiple files ouch decompress a.zip b.tar.gz c.tar ``` The `-d/--dir` flag can be used to redirect decompression results to another directory. ```sh # Decompress 'summer_vacation.zip' inside of new folder 'pictures' ouch decompress summer_vacation.zip --dir pictures ``` ## """Standard-library decompression operations for the ouch-compatible CLI."""
from __future__ import annotations
import bz2, gzip, lzma, os, shutil, tarfile, zipfile
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

_SINGLE = {'.gz': gzip.decompress, '.bz2': bz2.decompress, '.bz': bz2.decompress,
           '.xz': lzma.decompress, '.lzma': lzma.decompress}
_ALIASES = {
    '.tgz': '.tar.gz', '.tbz': '.tar.bz', '.tbz2': '.tar.bz2',
    '.tlz4': '.tar.lz4', '.txz': '.tar.xz', '.tlzma': '.tar.lzma',
    '.tsz': '.tar.sz', '.tzst': '.tar.zst', '.tlz': '.tar.lz', '.cbt': '.tar',
    '.cbz': '.zip', '.epub': '.zip', '.cb7': '.7z', '.cbr': '.rar',
}
_SUPPORTED = {'.tar','.zip','.7z','.gz','.bz','.bz2','.bz3','.xz','.lzma','.lz','.lzip','.lz4','.sz','.zst','.rar','.br',
              '.tar.gz','.tar.bz','.tar.bz2','.tar.bz3','.tar.xz','.tar.lzma','.tar.lz','.tar.lz4','.tar.sz','.tar.zst'}

def _strip_name(name: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    low = name.lower()
    for alias, expanded in _ALIASES.items():
        if low.endswith(alias):
            return name[:-len(alias)], expanded
    for ext in ('.tar.gz','.tar.bz2','.tar.bz','.tar.bz3','.tar.xz','.tar.lzma','.tar.lz4','.tar.sz','.tar.zst','.tar.lz','.tar'):
        if low.endswith(ext): return name[:-len(ext)], ext
    return os.path.splitext(name)[0], os.path.splitext(name)[1].lower()

def _archive_base(name: str) -> str:
    value=name
    lower=value.lower()
    for alias in _ALIASES:
        if lower.endswith(alias): return value[:-len(alias)]
    while True:
        suffix=Path(value).suffix.lower()
        if suffix not in _SINGLE and suffix not in {'.lz4','.lz','.lzip','.bz3','.sz','.zst','.br'}: break
        value=value[:-len(suffix)]
    lower=value.lower()
    for ext in ('.tar','.tgz','.tbz','.tbz2','.txz','.tlzma'):
        if lower.endswith(ext): return value[:-len(ext)]
    return os.path.splitext(value)[0]

def _safe_join(root: Path, member: str) -> Path:
    # Archive member paths are interpreted relative to destination, never outside it.
    clean = PurePosixPath(member.replace('\\', '/'))
    parts = [p for p in clean.parts if p not in ('/', '..', '.')]
    return root.joinpath(*parts)

def _check_contained(root: Path, dest: Path) -> None:
    """Reject a member whose parent resolves through an extracted symlink."""
    resolved_root = root.resolve()
    resolved_parent = dest.parent.resolve()
    try:
        resolved_parent.relative_to(resolved_root)
    except ValueError:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No such file or directory (os error 2) while canonicalizing {dest.parent}")

def _extract_tar(tf: tarfile.TarFile, root: Path) -> list[tuple[str,int]]:
    items=[]
    for m in tf.getmembers():
        dest=_safe_join(root,m.name)
        if m.isdir():
            _check_contained(root, dest)
            dest.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
            items.append((str(dest),None))
        elif m.isfile():
            _check_contained(root, dest)
            dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
            src=tf.extractfile(m)
            if src:
                with src, open(dest,'wb') as out: shutil.copyfileobj(src,out)
            try: os.chmod(dest,m.mode & 0o777)
            except OSError: pass

        elif m.issym():

            dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
            try:

            except OSError:

def _extract_zip(zf: zipfile.ZipFile, root: Path, password: str|None=None) -> list[tuple[str,int|None]]:
    items=[]
    for m in zf.infolist():
        dest=_safe_join(root,m.filename)
        if m.is_dir():
            dest.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
            items.append((str(dest),None))
            continue
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
        with zf.open(m, pwd=password.encode() if password else None) as src, open(dest,'wb') as out: shutil.copyfileobj(src,out)
        items.append((str(dest),m.file_size))
    return items

def decompress_one(filename: str, output_dir: str|None=None, here: bool=False, password: str|None=None, fmt: str|None=None, signature: bool=False) -> tuple[str,list[tuple[str,int|None]]]:
    src=Path(filename)
    data=src.read_bytes()
    base, ext=_strip_name(src.name)
    recognized_exts={'.tar','.tar.gz','.tar.bz','.tar.bz2','.tar.xz','.tar.lzma','.zip','.gz','.bz','.bz2','.xz','.lzma'}
    if fmt is None and ext not in recognized_exts:
        if zipfile.is_zipfile(src) or tarfile.is_tarfile(src) or data.startswith((b'\x1f\x8b', b'BZh', b'\xfd7zXZ')):
            base=src.stem + '-output'
    if signature:
        base=src.stem+'-output'
    if fmt:
        actual_ext=ext
        fmt_name=fmt.lower().lstrip('.')
        _, fmt_ext=_strip_name('format.'+fmt_name)
        known=_SUPPORTED
        if actual_ext not in known and not signature:
            base=src.name
        ext=fmt_ext
    is_tar = ext.startswith('.tar') or tarfile.is_tarfile(src)
    if ext == '.zip' or zipfile.is_zipfile(src):
        root=Path(output_dir) if output_dir is not None else (Path('.') if here else Path(base))
        root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
        try:
            with zipfile.ZipFile(src) as zf: entries=_extract_zip(zf,root,password)
        except zipfile.BadZipFile as exc:
            raise ValueError("Invalid zip archive\n - Could not find EOCD") from exc
        return str(root),entries
    if is_tar:
        root=Path(output_dir) if output_dir is not None else (Path('.') if here else Path(base))
        root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
        with tarfile.open(src,'r:*') as tf: entries=_extract_tar(tf,root)
        return str(root),entries
    if ext in _SINGLE:
        outpath=Path(output_dir) / Path(base).name if output_dir is not None else Path(base)
        if here and output_dir is None: outpath=Path(base)
        outpath.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
        decoded=_SINGLE[ext](data)
        # Chained stream compression: peel successive recognized extensions.
        remainder=Path(base).suffix.lower()
        while remainder in _SINGLE:
            decoded=_SINGLE[remainder](decoded)
            outpath=outpath.with_suffix('')
            remainder=outpath.suffix.lower()
        if decoded.startswith((b'PK\x03\x04',b'PK\x05\x06')):
            outpath.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
            with zipfile.ZipFile(__import__('io').BytesIO(decoded)) as zf: entries=_extract_zip(zf,outpath.parent)
            return str(outpath.parent),entries
        if len(decoded)>262 and decoded[257:262]==b'ustar':
            outpath.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
            root=Path(output_dir) if output_dir is not None else (Path('.') if here else Path(_archive_base(src.name)))
            root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
            with tarfile.open(fileobj=__import__('io').BytesIO(decoded),mode='r:*') as tf: entries=_extract_tar(tf,root)
            return str(root),entries

    raise ValueError(f"""Cannot decompress files

 - Decompression formats are detected automatically from file extension and signature

hint: Supported extensions are: tar, zip, bz, bz2, bz3, gz, lz4, xz, lzma, lz, sz, zst, rar, 7z
hint: Supported aliases are: tgz, tbz, tlz4, txz, tlzma, tsz, tzst, tlz, cbt, cbz, epub, cb7, cbr
hint: 
hint: Alternatively, you can pass an extension to the '--format' flag:
hint:   ouch decompress {src.name} --format tar.gz""")

def decompress_stdin(data: bytes, fmt: str|None=None, output_dir: str|None=None, here: bool=False) -> tuple[str,int|list[tuple[str,int|None]]]:
    """Decode compressed bytes from stdin into the conventional ouch-output file."""
    import io
    kind=(fmt or '').lower().lstrip('.')
    kind={'.tgz':'tar.gz','tgz':'tar.gz','tbz':'tar.bz','tbz2':'tar.bz2','txz':'tar.xz','tlzma':'tar.lzma','cbz':'zip','epub':'zip'}.get(kind,kind)
    if not kind:
        raise ValueError("""Cannot decompress files\n - Files with missing extensions: \"-\"\n - Decompression formats are detected automatically from file extension and signature\n\nhint: Supported extensions are: tar, zip, bz, bz2, bz3, gz, lz4, xz, lzma, lz, sz, zst, rar, 7z\nhint: Supported aliases are: tgz, tbz, tlz4, txz, tlzma, tsz, tzst, tlz, cbt, cbz, epub, cb7, cbr\nhint: \nhint: Alternatively, you can pass an extension to the '--format' flag:\nhint:   ouch decompress - --format tar.gz""")
    target=Path(output_dir or '.') / 'ouch-output'
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    if kind in ('gz','gzip'):
        try: decoded=gzip.decompress(data)
        except Exception as exc:
            if not data.startswith(b'\x1f\x8b'): raise ValueError('Failed to decompress -\n - invalid gzip header') from exc
            raise
    elif kind in ('bz','bz2'): decoded=bz2.decompress(data)
    elif kind in ('xz','lzma'): decoded=lzma.decompress(data)
    elif kind in ('zip','cbz','epub'):
        root=Path(output_dir or 'ouch-output') if not here else Path('.')
        root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as zf: entries=_extract_zip(zf,root)
        return str(root),entries
    elif kind.startswith('tar'):
        raw=data
        if kind.endswith('.gz') or kind=='tgz': raw=gzip.decompress(raw)
        elif kind.endswith(('.bz','.bz2')): raw=bz2.decompress(raw)
        elif kind.endswith(('.xz','.lzma')): raw=lzma.decompress(raw)
        root=Path(output_dir or 'ouch-output') if not here else Path('.')
        root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
        with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(raw),mode='r:*') as tf: entries=_extract_tar(tf,root)
        return str(root),entries
    else: raise ValueError('unsupported format: '+kind)
    target.write_bytes(decoded)
    return str(target),len(decoded)

def conflict_target(filename: str, output_dir: str|None=None, here: bool=False, fmt: str|None=None, signature: bool=False) -> str|None:
    """Return the existing output location that would trigger ouch's conflict prompt."""
    import zipfile
    src=Path(filename)
    base, ext=_strip_name(src.name)
    if signature:
        base=src.stem+'-output'
    if fmt:
        _, fmt_ext=_strip_name('format.'+fmt.lower().lstrip('.'))
        if ext not in _SUPPORTED:
            if not signature: base=src.name
        else:
            base=_archive_base(src.name)
        ext=fmt_ext
    else:
        base=_archive_base(src.name)
    members=None
    if zipfile.is_zipfile(src):
        with zipfile.ZipFile(src) as zf:
            members=[(i.filename,i.is_dir()) for i in zf.infolist()]
    else:
        try:
            with tarfile.open(src,'r:*') as tf:
                members=[(m.name,m.isdir()) for m in tf.getmembers()]
        except (tarfile.TarError,OSError):
            pass
    if members is not None:
        if here and output_dir is None:
            return None
        root=Path(output_dir) if output_dir is not None else (Path('.') if here else Path(base))
        if root.exists() and not root.is_dir():
            return str(root)
        if root.is_dir():
            for name,_is_dir in members:
                if _safe_join(root,name).exists():
                    return str(root)
        return None
    if ext in _SINGLE:
        if output_dir is not None and Path(output_dir).exists() and not Path(output_dir).is_dir():
            return output_dir
        target=Path(output_dir)/Path(base).name if output_dir is not None else Path(base)
        return str(target) if target.exists() else None
    return None

def detect_format(filename: str) -> str|None:
    """Infer a common archive codec from its file signature."""
    data=Path(filename).read_bytes()[:512]
    if data.startswith(b'\x1f\x8b'): return 'gz'
    if data.startswith(b'BZh'): return 'bz2'
    if data.startswith(b'\xfd7zXZ\x00'): return 'xz'
    if data.startswith(b'PK\x03\x04') or data.startswith(b'PK\x05\x06'): return 'zip'
    if len(data)>=262 and data[257:262]==b'ustar': return 'tar'
    return None

def unsupported_format_error(filename: str) -> str:
    absolute=os.path.abspath(filename)
    relative=os.path.relpath(absolute,os.getcwd())
    name=absolute if relative == '..' or relative.startswith('..'+os.sep) else relative
    extension=Path(name).suffix
    kind='unsupported' if extension else 'missing'
    return (f'Cannot decompress files\n - Files with {kind} extensions: "{name}"\n'
            ' - Decompression formats are detected automatically from file extension and signature\n\n'
            'hint: Supported extensions are: tar, zip, bz, bz2, bz3, gz, lz4, xz, lzma, lz, sz, zst, rar, 7z\n'
            'hint: Supported aliases are: tgz, tbz, tlz4, txz, tlzma, tsz, tzst, tlz, cbt, cbz, epub, cb7, cbr\n'
            'hint: \nhint: Alternatively, you can pass an extension to the \'--format\' flag:\n'
            f'hint:   ouch decompress {name} --format tar.gz')
"}]
